title: Basie's small 1937 band: heads, personnel and size
summary: Edison explains why he quit over head arrangements and lists the band's trombones and four saxophones.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Well, the only trouble with the heads is the personnel changes.

Oh, yeah. That's the reason why I quit that time. Because, you know, when I joined the band they had already played these arrangements for years with Benny Moten. You see. And I was scruffling and trying to use a little ingenuity that I did have to find a note to play an arrangement and Basie said, "Well, when you do that and you find a note tonight and it sounds good, play the same damn note tomorrow night, every night." Every night, you know.
Well, when you joined were Dicky Wells and Benny Moton there?
He wasn't in the band. Dan Minor was in the band. And -- Dan Minor, and let's see, who else? Dicky Wells
came later.
Did Benny Morton come before Dicky?
I can't remember.
Yeah. Yeah, we only had two trombones. Three trumpets and two trombones.
Eddie Durham was gone when you joined them?

Yeah, he was just getting ready to leave. But he was playing trombone and guitar, you know. Solo guitar. We had Dan Minor, I forget who the other trombone player was. When I joined the band, Dicky Wells was the chief player. He was with Teddy Hill. And Benny Morton was still with Don Redman. That's 1937, he was still with Don Redman. And we had Dan Minor. I don't think we had but one trombone, full brass.
Well, of course, that's another thing, you know, that --
We had four saxophones. We didn't even have five at the time. We had two tenors and two altos.
Well, wasn't Jack Washington in then?
Yeah, he played alto and tenor, though. Alto and baritones.
Most of the time he was playing alto?
Right. Alto and baritone. See, they had Earl Warren, they had Jack Washington, Herschel and Lester.
Had four saxophones.
Well, you know, as you add that fifth saxophone, and you have the baritone --
Yeah, see, we finally added another alto and Jack played strictly baritone because he loved baritone, you see. He was a Harry Carney fan.
He was good, though, wasn't he?
Oh, was he good. He could play.
record out of They put a / the band did the Famous Door, you know, for broadcast recently and there's a lot of solos by him.
Oh, yeah, he was a good baritone player. And a good alto player.
But you see, when you have just four saxes there, two altos, and you had one trombone, so the band had a lighter sound.
Oh, definitely.

And to my mind, when they added -- they get five saxophones and then they get three and four trombones and they get up to four trumpets, it begins to get a much better ensemble sound. But the thing is getting stiffer.
